prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create one high-fidelity polished desktop website screenshot, landscape 1440 by 1080 composition, front-facing flat UI with no device frame, one first viewport plus a glimpse below the fold. Product: Spironolactone Atlas. This is a conventional clinical-editorial category-standard decision concept, played straight with equal craft to a professional published medical education site.
SURFACE STRUCTURE IN ORDER:
1. Slim top navigation 84px tall, constrained to 1248px width with generous margins. Left small serif wordmark “Spironolactone Atlas”; right clear links “The story”, “Reporting data”, “Evidence”, “Methods”, and a simple outward arrow “Sources”.
2. Large comfortable centered hero on warm off-white. Tiny spaced mono eyebrow “AN EDUCATIONAL EVIDENCE ATLAS”. One dominant centered Fraunces-like display serif heading “Spironolactone Atlas” at approximately 90px, dark ink. Under it a brief centered clean Inter-style 22px paragraph across about 760px: “A guided look at spironolactone uses, research evidence and adverse-event reporting.” Then smaller sentence “Understand the story. Explore the sources. See the limits.” Two clear centered actions side by side: solid dark ink rectangular button with slightly softened 5px corners “Read the story” and arrow, outlined secondary “Explore data”. No excessively huge empty hero; all four stat panels fit comfortably in the first view.
3. Four equal familiar headline statistic panels in a neat row across content width, separated by subtle ink hairlines, near y550. Low-key warm white fill, fine borders and restrained 6px corners, precise typographic hierarchy. Panel one large mono “24,805”, label “Selected reports”; panel two large mono “2004–2025”, label “Reporting window”; panel three large mono “3,452”, label “Hyperkalaemia mentions”; panel four large mono “52.2%”, label “No informative indication”. Each stat correctly describes reporting observations, never prevalence or incidence. Beneath row a small clearly readable source caption “Source: openFDA · Retrieved 3 Nov 2026 · Selected cohort: 24,805 reports”.
4. First lower chart section starts near y800 so heading and entire three-bar chart appear in the glimpse below-fold. Thin horizontal divider. Left 35% column heading in tasteful display serif “What appears in the reports?” and sentence “Reaction terms are counted within the selected reporting cohort.” Right 65% simple professional horizontal bar chart with precise text labels: “Hyperkalaemia” value “3,452”, “Acute kidney injury” value “3,133”, “Hypotension” value “1,832”. Bars lengths faithfully proportional 100%, 90.8%, 53.1%. First bar coral #F48F7A, second and third muted teal #65B8AC. Chart is legible, typography aligned, tiny source “openFDA · Denominator: 24,805 selected reports”. At lower edge show understated educational caveat “Educational use. Reporting is not incidence or causality.”
VISUAL SYSTEM: palette pinned dark ink #0B1020, warm off-white #F3F0E8, coral #F48F7A and teal #65B8AC. Predominantly off-white editorial surface with ink type and restrained coral/teal data accents. Fraunces-like confident serif display, exceptionally readable Inter-like body, mono/tabular data. Familiar centered hierarchy, steady 8px spacing, orderly comfortable content widths, crisp fine rules, no gritty textures, restrained panel elevation. Match the professionalism of a calm scientific editorial reading site, complete and resolved.
ACCURACY CONSTRAINTS: Only the supplied numbers and content, no invented author names, claims, testimonials, dates, prices, research benchmarks, badges, or medical advice. Reporting is not incidence or causality. No physiology illustration, fake microscopy, stock photography, pills, floating molecules, anatomy, or decorative science graphics. Do not use experimental asymmetric or brutalist layouts. No design-process labels in screenshot. This is the website itself. Accurate legible copy, excellent spacing and hierarchy.
deviations: Native generated dimensions 1487x1058; approximate requested desktop aspect.
